title: UML Sequence Diagram
intro: Sequence diagrams show which objects talk to each other, with which messages, and in what order. Quiz questions ask you to read the arrows and fragments, and to turn a diagram into Java code or Java code into a diagram.

cards.title: What a sequence diagram shows
cards.body:
A **sequence diagram** (behavioural UML) shows the objects in one scenario and the **messages** they exchange, **in time order**.
The whole diagram sits in a **frame**. The pentagon tag in the top-left corner holds `sd` + the interaction name, e.g. `sd ButtonPress`.
The objects go across the top. **Time runs downward.**

cards.title: Lifelines: who takes part
cards.body:
Each participant is a **lifeline**: a head box plus a **dashed vertical line** that shows the participant's lifetime.
The head label has the format `[name] : ClassName`. **`:ClassName` is mandatory**; the object name in front is optional.
So `ol:OrderLine` (named) and `:Product` (anonymous) are both fine, but `Product` alone is not. A human user can be drawn as a stick-figure actor.

cards.title: Activation bars
cards.body:
A thin rectangle on a lifeline is an **activation** (execution specification): the period when that object is **running a method**.
It starts when a message arrives and ends when the method returns.
A **self-call** puts a second, slightly offset bar on top of the first, because the outer method is still running while the inner one runs.

cards.title: Walkthrough: sequence diagram to Java
cards.body:
Read every arrow and ask: **which lifeline does the arrowhead point INTO?** That class must have the method. The sender's method makes the call.

1. **Head without a colon**: `Cart` is not valid. Write `:Cart` or `c:Cart`.
2. **Solid reply**: a reply is always **dashed**.
3. **Created object at the top**: its head must sit where the `new` arrow arrives.
4. **Wrong owner**: the method belongs to the class the arrowhead points INTO. The sender only calls it.
5. Using `alt` for an `if` with no else: use `opt`. And `loop(10)` means 10 times, not 9.
